questions.question: Which of the following initiatives did the Maharashtra Government approve in September 2025 to generate employment in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities and boost skilled job opportunities?

options.text: Free Urban Transit Support Scheme for job seekers
Targeted Wage Subsidy Programme for unskilled labourers
Global Capability Center policy to expand centres across the state
Mandatory Local Employment Reservation framework in enterprises

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Global Capability Center policy to expand centres across the state**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Maharashtra Government**, in **September 2025**, approved the **Global Capability Center (GCC) Policy** to position the state as a leading destination for high-value technical and administrative operations.
 
• The policy specifically targets the development of **Tier-2** and **Tier-3** cities like **Nagpur**, **Nashik**, **Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar**, and **Pune** to decentralize industrial growth away from the saturated **Mumbai** Metropolitan Region. ***Hence, the correct answer is Global Capability Center policy to expand centres across the state.***
 
• The initiative aims to generate approximately **1 million (10 lakh)** high-skilled jobs by the year **2030**, focusing on **knowledge-based industries**.
 
• Under this policy, the state offers significant incentives, including **stamp duty exemptions**, **electricity duty waivers**, and **investment subsidies** to multinational corporations (MNCs) setting up their centers of excellence.
 
• The focus of these centers will be on cutting-edge technologies such as **Artificial Intelligence (AI)**, **Machine Learning (ML)**, **Data Analytics**, and **Blockchain**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Understanding Global Capability Centers (GCCs)**: 
 
 
• **GCCs** are offshore units established by **multinational corporations** to handle specialized tasks including **Research and Development (R&D)**, **IT support**, and **Finance/HR operations**.
 
• India has evolved from being a "back-office" hub to a "global innovation hub," currently housing over **1,600 GCCs** that contribute significantly to the **GDP**.
 
 
 
• **Economic Significance**: 
 
 
• The **GCC sector** in India is projected to reach a market size of **$110 billion** by **2030**.
 
• Maharashtra’s policy is a strategic move to capture a lion's share of this market, contributing to India’s goal of becoming a **$5 trillion economy**.
 
 
 
• **Urban Development**: 
 
 
• By focusing on **Tier-2** and **Tier-3** cities, the government aims to improve **infrastructure**, **real estate**, and the **local service economy** in these regions.
 
• This shift helps in reducing the **cost of operations** for companies while providing **local employment** to graduates within their home districts.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Skill Integration**: The policy involves collaboration with the **Maharashtra State Skill Development Society (MSSDS)** to create a curriculum tailored to the specific needs of **GCCs**.
 
• **Plug-and-Play Facilities**: To attract fast-paced investments, the state is developing **IT parks** and **Knowledge Parks** with **plug-and-play** infrastructure, allowing companies to start operations immediately.
 
• **Sustainability**: The policy encourages **green building** practices and the use of **renewable energy** within these new capability centers to align with **ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance)** goals.
 
• **Single-Window Clearance**: To improve the **Ease of Doing Business**, a dedicated cell has been established to provide **single-window clearances** for all regulatory requirements related to **GCCs**.

questions.question: In March 2025, who inaugurated the two-day National Conference on ‘Environment – 2025’ in New Delhi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **President of India**, **Smt. Droupadi Murmu**, inaugurated the two-day **National Conference on ‘Environment – 2025’** held in **New Delhi** in **March 2025**.
 
• The conference was organized to address the pressing **global environmental challenges** and to formulate a roadmap for **sustainable development** in the coming decade.
 
• During the inauguration, the **President** highlighted the urgent need for **climate justice** and the protection of **biodiversity**, emphasizing that humanity's survival depends on a healthy planet.
 
• The event served as a high-level forum bringing together **environmentalists**, **scientists**, **policymakers**, and **judicial experts** to discuss the integration of **traditional ecological knowledge** with **modern science**.
 
• The conference focused on India's progress toward achieving its **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)** under the **Paris Agreement** and the country's commitment to reaching **Net Zero** carbon emissions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC):**
 
 
• This is the nodal agency of the **Central Government** responsible for the planning and coordination of **India's environmental policies**.
 
• The ministry oversees the implementation of various acts such as the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986** and the **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972**.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Mandate:**
 
 
• **Article 48A**: A **Directive Principle of State Policy** which states that the State shall endeavor to protect and improve the **environment** and to safeguard the **forests** and **wildlife** of the country.
 
• **Article 51A(g)**: A **Fundamental Duty** of every citizen to protect and improve the natural environment including **forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife**.
 
 
 
• **Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment):**
 
 
• Launched by the **Prime Minister of India**, this initiative promotes a **circular economy** and encourages individuals to adopt sustainable lifestyles to mitigate **climate change**.
 
• It aims to replace the prevalent 'use-and-dispose' economy with a 'circular economy' defined by mindful and deliberate utilization.
 
 
 
• **National Green Tribunal (NGT):**
 
 
• Established in **2010** under the **NGT Act**, it is a specialized body equipped with the necessary expertise to handle **environmental disputes** involving multi-disciplinary issues.
 
• It provides a fast-track mechanism for cases related to **environmental protection** and conservation of forests.
 
 
 
• **International Solar Alliance (ISA):**
 
 
• Headquartered in **Gurugram, India**, this alliance was jointy launched by **India** and **France** to mobilize efforts against **climate change** through the deployment of **solar energy** solutions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Panchamrit Strategy**: At **COP26**, India announced five nectar elements (**Panchamrit**) to deal with **climate change**, including reaching **500 GW** of non-fossil energy capacity by **2030**.
 
• **Carbon Credit Trading Scheme**: India is developing its own **carbon market** to incentivize **greenhouse gas** emission reductions and promote **green technology**.
 
• **World Environment Day**: Celebrated annually on **June 5**, it serves as the principal vehicle of the **United Nations** for encouraging awareness and action for the protection of the **environment**.

questions.question: When did Larsen & Toubro (L&T) launch the Indian Navy’s Second Multi-Purpose Vessel (MPV)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**January 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Larsen & Toubro (L&T)** achieved a significant milestone by launching the **second Multi-Purpose Vessel (MPV)** for the **Indian Navy** on **January 16, 2025**.
 
• The vessel, named **‘Samarthak’**, was launched at **L&T’s Kattupalli Shipyard** located near **Chennai**, **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• The launch ceremony was graced by **Smt. Tanvi Singh**, who performed the traditional honors, in the presence of **Vice Admiral Krishna Swaminathan**, the **Vice Chief of Naval Staff**.
 
• This vessel is the second in a series of **two MPVs** being constructed by **L&T** under a contract signed with the **Ministry of Defence** in **March 2022**.
 
• The first vessel of this class, named **‘Vayan’**, was launched earlier in **September 2024**, demonstrating the rapid pace of construction at the shipyard.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vessel Role and Capabilities:**
 
 
• The **Multi-Purpose Vessels (MPVs)** are designed to perform a wide array of roles including **maritime surveillance**, **towing of targets**, and acting as a platform for **naval training**.
 
• They are also equipped to provide **Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR)**, making them vital assets for non-combat maritime operations.
 
• The ships feature advanced **indigenous equipment** and systems, aligning with the **‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’** (Self-reliant India) initiative.
 
 
 
• **Technical Specifications:**
 
 
• The vessels are approximately **106 meters** in length and **15 meters** in width.
 
• They are capable of reaching a maximum speed of **15 knots** and have an endurance suited for prolonged deployments in the **Indian Ocean Region (IOR)**.
 
• The contract for these **two vessels** was valued at approximately **Rs. 887 crore**.
 
 
 
• **L&T Shipbuilding:**
 
 
• **L&T** is a major private player in **India's defense manufacturing** sector, specifically in naval shipbuilding.
 
• The **Kattupalli Shipyard** is a state-of-the-art facility that has delivered several **Interceptor Boats**, **Offshore Patrol Vessels (OPVs)**, and **Floating Docks** to the **Indian Navy** and **Indian Coast Guard**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Strategic Significance:** The induction of **MPVs** like **Samarthak** will allow the **Indian Navy** to phase out aging auxiliary ships and enhance its auxiliary fleet's operational efficiency.
 
• **Launch vs Commissioning:** While the **launch** occurred in **January 2025**, the vessel will now undergo a series of **sea trials** and equipment fit-outs before being formally **commissioned** into active service.
 
• **Timeline:** The delivery of both vessels is planned to be completed within a **36-month** window from the start of the project, highlighting the efficiency of **indigenous private shipyards**.

questions.question: Which of the following ministries announced the fourth phase of amalgamation of RRBs in April 2025 under the 'One State, One RRB' policy to enhance the operational efficiency of regional rural banks (RRBs)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Finance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Finance** has officially set the stage for the **fourth phase** of **Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) amalgamation**, which is scheduled to commence in **April 2025**.
 
• This initiative is driven by the **'One State, One RRB'** policy, aiming to consolidate multiple **RRBs** operating within the same state into a single, robust entity to reduce administrative overheads.
 
• The primary objective of this reorganization is to **enhance operational efficiency**, improve **cost-to-income ratios**, and leverage **economies of scale** to better serve the rural population.
 
• Under this plan, the total number of **RRBs** in **India** is projected to be reduced from the existing **43** to approximately **28**, ensuring a more streamlined banking structure.
 
• The **Department of Financial Services (DFS)**, under the **Ministry of Finance**, is the nodal agency coordinating with **Sponsor Banks** and **State Governments** to finalize the roadmap for this consolidation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **History of RRBs**: **Regional Rural Banks** were established under the provisions of an Ordinance passed in **September 1975** and the **RRB Act of 1976**, following the recommendations of the **Narasimham Committee**. The first **RRB**, **Prathama Bank**, was established on **October 2, 1975**.
 
• **Shareholding Pattern**: The equity of an **RRB** is held by three parties in a fixed proportion: the **Central Government (50%)**, the **Sponsor Bank (35%)**, and the concerned **State Government (15%)**.
 
• **Phases of Consolidation**: 
 
 
• **Phase 1 (2005)**: Amalgamation of **RRBs** sponsored by the same bank within a state.
 
• **Phase 2 (2012)**: Amalgamation of **RRBs** across different sponsor banks within a state.
 
• **Phase 3 (2019)**: Further consolidation reduced the count to **43** to improve financial viability.
 
 
 
• **Regulation and Supervision**: While **RRBs** are regulated by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, their supervisory powers are vested in the **National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)**.
 
• **Mandate**: **RRBs** are required to provide **75%** of their total credit to the **Priority Sector Lending (PSL)** categories, which is higher than the **40%** requirement for **Scheduled Commercial Banks**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Operational Efficiency**: The **'One State, One RRB'** model helps in **technology integration** and uniform **banking practices** across the state, making it easier for the **Sponsor Banks** to manage operations.
 
• **Financial Health**: Consolidation often leads to better **Capital to Risk-weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR)** and helps weaker **RRBs** benefit from the financial strength of stronger ones within the same geography.
 
• **Geographic Presence**: Despite the reduction in the total number of banks, the **branch network** in **rural** and **semi-urban** areas remains intact or expands, ensuring that **financial inclusion** goals are not compromised.
</ul

questions.question: India observed World No Tobacco Day on which date in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**31 May**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **World No Tobacco Day** is observed globally every year on **31 May** to create awareness about the harmful and deadly effects of tobacco use and exposure to second-hand smoke.
 
• The initiative was first started by the **World Health Organization (WHO)** in **1987** to draw global attention to the tobacco epidemic and the preventable death and disease it causes.
 
• The **World Health Assembly** passed **Resolution WHA42.19** in **1988**, which formally called for the celebration of **World No Tobacco Day** every year on **31 May**.
 
• In **2025**, **India** continues its active participation in this global campaign, led by the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW)**, to strengthen tobacco control measures and protect the younger generation from nicotine addiction.
 
• The day serves as a call to action, advocating for effective policies to reduce tobacco consumption and engaging stakeholders across various sectors to join the fight against the tobacco industry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tobacco Control Legislation in India:**
 
 
• The **Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act (COTPA)**, passed in **2003**, is the primary law that regulates the advertisement, production, and distribution of tobacco products in **India**.
 
• **Section 4** of **COTPA** prohibits smoking in **public places**, while **Section 6** prohibits the sale of tobacco products to **minors** (below **18 years** of age) and within **100 yards** of educational institutions.
 
 
 
• **Health and Economic Impact:**
 
 
• Tobacco use is a major risk factor for non-communicable diseases (NCDs) including **lung cancer**, **cardiovascular diseases**, and **chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)**.
 
• According to the **Global Adult Tobacco Survey (GATS)**, **India** has one of the highest numbers of tobacco users globally, which imposes a massive economic burden due to healthcare costs and lost productivity.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The **National Tobacco Control Programme (NTCP)** was launched by the **Government of India** in **2007-08** with the aim of creating awareness and ensuring effective implementation of **COTPA** provisions.
 
• In **September 2019**, the Indian government enacted the **Prohibition of Electronic Cigarettes Act** to ban the production, import, sale, and advertisement of **e-cigarettes** to prevent health risks to the youth.
 
 
 
• **WHO MPOWER Measures:**
 
 
• The **WHO** introduced the **MPOWER** package to help countries implement the **WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (WHO FCTC)**.
 
• This includes **Monitoring** tobacco use, **Protecting** people from smoke, **Offering** help to quit, **Warning** about dangers, **Enforcing** bans on advertising, and **Raising** taxes on tobacco.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Statistics:** Tobacco kills more than **8 million** people each year, including an estimated **1.3 million** non-smokers who are exposed to **second-hand smoke**.
 
• **Tobacco Cultivation:** **India** is the **second-largest** producer of tobacco in the world, with states like **Andhra Pradesh**, **Gujarat**, and **Karnataka** being the primary hubs for its cultivation.
 
• **Constitutional Provision:** **Article 47** of the **Constitution of India** directs the State to endeavor to bring about the prohibition of the consumption of intoxicating drinks and of drugs which are injurious to health, providing a basis for tobacco control.
</ul

questions.question: At the Taiwan Athletics Open, which took place in Taipei on 7 and 8 June 2025, how many total medals did India win?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**16**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian athletics contingent** concluded their campaign at the **Taiwan Athletics Open**, held in **Taipei** on **7 and 8 June 2025**, with a total of **16 medals**.
 
• Out of the total **16 medals**, the Indian athletes secured **7 Gold**, **6 Silver**, and **3 Bronze** medals across various track and field events.
 
• The event took place at the **Taipei Municipal Stadium** in **Chinese Taipei**, serving as a significant international exposure for the athletes to improve their **world rankings**.
 
• On the **opening day** of the competition, India made a strong start by clinching **seven medals**, which set the tone for the final tally of **16**.
 
• Leading the charge were prominent athletes such as **D.P. Manu** in javelin and **Jyothi Yarraji** in hurdles, both of whom secured top podium finishes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Individual Gold Medalists**:
 
 
• **D.P. Manu** won the **Gold medal** in the **men's javelin throw** with a best effort of **81.58 meters**, reaffirming his position as one of India's top throwers.
 
• **Jyothi Yarraji** clinched the **Gold** in the **women's 100m hurdles**, clocking a time of **13.23 seconds** to dominate the field.
 
• **Kiran Pahal** secured the **Gold** in the **women's 400m** race with a timing of **52.51 seconds**.
 
• In the **shot put** events, **Tajinderpal Singh Toor** (men) and **Abha Khatua** (women) both brought home **Gold medals** with throws of **19.17 meters** and **17.56 meters** respectively.
 
 
 
• **Silver and Bronze Contributions**:
 
 
• **Nithya Ramraj** finished just behind Jyothi Yarraji to take the **Silver medal** in the **women's 100m hurdles**, making it a 1-2 finish for India.
 
• The **men's 4x400m relay team** and other specialized track athletes contributed significantly to the **6 Silver** and **3 Bronze** count, ensuring India finished high in the overall standings.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of the Event**: The **Taiwan Athletics Open** is a **World Athletics Continental Tour Bronze** level meet, which is crucial for athletes aiming to accumulate **ranking points** for major championships like the **World Athletics Championships** and the **Olympics**.
 
• **Performance Consistency**: The **16-medal haul** reflects the growing depth in **Indian athletics**, particularly in technical events like **javelin throw** and **shot put**, as well as sprint hurdles.
 
• **Key Participants**: Other notable participants included **Nayana James**, who won **Gold** in the **women's long jump**, contributing to the dominant **7 Gold** medal tally.
 
• **Administrative Body**: The participation was facilitated by the **Athletics Federation of India (AFI)** to ensure that elite athletes maintain competitive rhythm during the international season.

questions.question: In July 2025, DRDO successfully conducted two consecutive successful flight tests of the Pralay missile at which of the following locations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Island**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **July 2025**, the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** successfully carried out two consecutive flight tests of the **Pralay** missile.
 
• The tests were conducted from the **Integrated Test Range (ITR)** located at **Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Island**, off the coast of **Odisha**.
 
• **Pralay** is a **surface-to-surface**, **short-range ballistic missile (SRBM)** developed for battlefield use by the **Indian Army**.
 
• The missile was tested for different ranges and demonstrated high-level accuracy by hitting the designated target with precision, meeting all mission objectives.
 
• During these flight tests, all subsystems performed satisfactorily, and the **missile's trajectory** was monitored by various **range sensors**, including **Radar**, **Electro-Optical Tracking System**, and **Telemetry** stations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Missile Specifications and Features:**
 
 
• **Pralay** is a **solid-fuel**, **quasi-ballistic** missile that has been developed to follow a path that makes it difficult for enemy **interceptor missiles** to track and destroy.
 
• It has a strike range of **150 to 500 kilometers** and can carry a payload of **350 kg to 1000 kg**.
 
• The missile is powered by a **solid-propellant rocket motor** and incorporates several new technologies, including state-of-the-art **navigation** and **integrated avionics**.
 
• It is designed to be launched from a **mobile launcher**, providing high strategic flexibility to the armed forces.
 
 
 
• **Geographic Location of the Test Site:**
 
 
• **Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Island**, formerly known as **Wheeler Island**, is situated in the **Bay of Bengal**, approximately **10 kilometers** off the coast of **Odisha** in the **Bhadrak district**.
 
• It serves as the primary missile testing facility for India, where most of the **Agni** and **Prithvi** series missiles are flight-tested.
 
• The island was renamed in **September 2015** to honor the late Indian President and scientist, **Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam**.
 
 
 
• **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO):**
 
 
• **DRDO** is the premier R&D organization under the **Ministry of Defence**, Government of India.
 
• It was established in **1958** by merging the Technical Development Establishment (TDEs) of the Indian Army and the Directorate of Technical Development & Production (DTDP) with the Defence Science Organisation (DSO).
 
• The organization is headquartered in **New Delhi** and works toward achieving self-reliance in critical defense technologies and systems.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Strategic Importance:** The **Pralay** missile is intended to provide India with a significant **counter-force** capability against **long-range artillery** and **tactical ballistic missiles** of adversaries.
 
• **Comparison:** Experts often compare **Pralay** to the **Russian Iskander** and **Chinese Dongfeng 12** missiles due to its ability to change its path mid-air to evade defense systems.
 
• **Other Locations Mentioned:**
 
 
• **Chandipur:** Another prominent site of the **Integrated Test Range (ITR)** in **Odisha**, typically used for testing **short-range missiles**, **rockets**, and **surface-to-air missiles** like **Akash**.
 
• **Pokhran:** Located in the **Jaisalmer** district of **Rajasthan**, it is famous as the site for India’s **nuclear tests** (1974 and 1998) and is also used for testing **artillery guns** and **tanks**.
 
• **Balasore:** The district in **Odisha** that houses the **Integrated Test Range** facilities at **Chandipur**.
 
 
 
• **Technology:** The **Pralay** missile uses a **canister-based** launch system, which allows for faster deployment and longer shelf-life by protecting the missile from environmental degradation.

questions.question: Which Indian actress was named National Ambassador for Cyber Safety by Ministry of Home Affairs in October 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rashmika Mandanna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **October 2024**, the **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** appointed popular Indian actress **Rashmika Mandanna** as the **National Ambassador for Cyber Safety**.
 
• The appointment was facilitated through the **Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C)**, which is the specialized wing of the **MHA** tasked with handling cyber-related offenses.
 
• The primary objective of this collaboration is to strengthen the fight against **cybercrime** by raising awareness about **online safety**, **digital hygiene**, and the dangers of **deepfake technology**.
 
• As the **National Ambassador**, she will lead various nationwide campaigns to educate citizens on how to protect their **digital identity** and navigate the **internet** securely.
 
• The initiative specifically focuses on reaching the youth and vulnerable sections of society who are increasingly targeted by **cyber fraudsters** and **malicious AI-generated content**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C):**
 
 
• Established in **2018** by the **Ministry of Home Affairs**, **I4C** provides a framework and ecosystem for **Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs)** to deal with cybercrimes in a coordinated manner.
 
• It operates the **National Cybercrime Reporting Portal** (**www.cybercrime.gov.in**), which allows victims to report **financial frauds** and **crimes against women and children** online.
 
• The centre also manages the **National Cybercrime Helpline Number 1930**, which provides immediate assistance to victims of **cyber financial fraud**.
 
 
 
• **Context of the Appointment:**
 
 
• **Rashmika Mandanna** became a vocal advocate for **cyber legislation** after she was targeted by a viral **deepfake video** in late **2023**.
 
• Her personal experience with **identity theft** and **AI misuse** makes her a relatable figure for the **CyberSafe India** campaign, emphasizing the importance of **legal protection** and **strict reporting**.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) Role:**
 
 
• Under the leadership of Union Home Minister **Shri Amit Shah**, the **MHA** has prioritized **cybersecurity** as a critical component of **national security**.

questions.question: At which summit did India’s NSA Ajit Doval push for a unified counter‑terrorism stance in June 2025?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the meeting of the National Security Advisers (NSAs) of the **Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)** held in **China** in **June 2025**, India’s NSA **Ajit Doval** strongly advocated for a **unified counter-terrorism stance** among member nations.
 
• He emphasized that the **SCO** must strictly adhere to the principle of **zero tolerance** for terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, including **cross-border terrorism** and the financing of terror activities.
 
• NSA **Ajit Doval** called for the strengthening of the **Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS)**, which is the permanent organ of the **SCO** headquartered in **Tashkent**, to enhance **intelligence sharing** and technical cooperation.
 
• He also highlighted the rising threat of **cyber-terrorism** and the use of **emerging technologies** like **drones** and **artificial intelligence** by terror groups, urging the **SCO** to develop a collaborative framework to counter these **asymmetric threats**.
 
• The **June 2025** summit served as a platform where **India** reiterated its stand on **territorial integrity** and **sovereignty**, particularly concerning **connectivity projects** within the **Eurasian** region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO):**

• The current members include **China**, **Russia**, **India**, **Pakistan**, **Kazakhstan**, **Kyrgyzstan**, **Tajikistan**, **Uzbekistan**, and **Iran**.

• **EU Summit:**

• **India** engages with the **EU** through **India-EU Summits**, but the primary security focus for **NSA Ajit Doval** in **June 2025** was the **Eurasian** security architecture. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***

questions.question: During COP30 held in November 2025, the term Conference of the Parties (COP) refers to the meeting of the Parties under which United Nations convention?

options.text: United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity (UNCBD)
Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES)
United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Conference of the Parties (COP)** serves as the supreme decision-making body of the **United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)**. It is responsible for reviewing the implementation of the Convention and any other legal instruments adopted by the body.
 
• **COP30** is scheduled to be held in **November 2025**. The host city for this milestone event is **Belém**, **Brazil**, marking a significant return of the climate summit to the **Amazon** region.
 
• The primary mandate of the **UNFCCC** is to achieve the stabilization of **greenhouse gas** concentrations in the atmosphere at a level that would prevent dangerous anthropogenic interference with the climate system.
 
• During these annual meetings, representatives from **198 Parties** (197 countries plus the European Union) gather to negotiate climate actions, assess progress, and refine strategies such as the **Paris Agreement**.
 
• The designation **COP30** specifically refers to the **30th** session of the Conference of the Parties to the **UNFCCC**. While other conventions like **UNCBD** also use the term COP, their numbering and meeting cycles differ. ***Hence, the correct answer is United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **UNFCCC Origins:** The convention was adopted on **May 9, 1992**, and was opened for signature at the **Earth Summit** in **Rio de Janeiro**, **Brazil**. It officially entered into force on **March 21, 1994**.
 
• **Major Agreements:** The **UNFCCC** provides the framework for two major international treaties: the **Kyoto Protocol (1997)** and the **Paris Agreement (2015)**. The **Paris Agreement** aims to limit the global temperature increase to well below **2 degrees Celsius** above pre-industrial levels.
 
• **UNCBD (United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity):** This is a separate "Rio Convention" focused on the conservation of biological diversity and the sustainable use of its components. Its COPs usually occur **biennially** (every two years).
 
• **CITES:** The **Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora** is an international agreement between governments to ensure that international trade in specimens of wild animals and plants does not threaten the survival of the species.
 
• **UNCAC:** The **United Nations Convention Against Corruption** is the only legally binding universal anti-corruption instrument, managed by the **UNODC**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of COP30:** **COP30** in **2025** is considered a critical juncture because parties are expected to submit their updated **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)**, which are the climate action plans to cut emissions and adapt to climate impacts.
 
• **Historical Context:** The first-ever COP (**COP1**) was held in **Berlin**, **Germany**, in **1995**. Since then, the meeting has rotated annually among the **five recognized UN regions**: Africa, Asia-Pacific, Eastern Europe, Latin America and the Caribbean, and Western Europe and Others.
 
• **The Secretariat:** The **UN Climate Change Secretariat** is the United Nations entity tasked with supporting the global response to the threat of climate change. It is located in **Bonn**, **Germany**.
 
• **Financial Mechanisms:** To support developing countries, the **UNFCCC** operates financial mechanisms including the **Global Environment Facility (GEF)** and the **Green Climate Fund (GCF)**.

• At the age of **37**, the **Serbian** tennis legend surpassed the previous record for longevity at this elite level of competition, which was notably held by **Roger Federer**.

questions.question: As per Human Development Index (HDI) 2025, what is the rank of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**130th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India has been ranked **130th** in the **Human Development Index (HDI)** for the year **2025**.
 
• The **Human Development Index (HDI)** is a composite statistical tool used to rank countries by level of "human development" and is released annually by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**.
 
• The ranking is based on a score that reflects achievements in key dimensions of human development, placing India within the **Medium Human Development** category among the **193 countries** and territories evaluated.
 
• The index considers several critical indicators, including **life expectancy at birth**, **expected years of schooling**, **mean years of schooling**, and **Gross National Income (GNI) per capita**.
 
• India's position at **130th** signifies the ongoing transition and progress in social and economic parameters, though it highlights the need for further improvements in healthcare and educational infrastructure compared to global leaders.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dimensions of HDI:**
 
 
• **Long and Healthy Life**: This is measured by **Life Expectancy at Birth**. It reflects the overall health and quality of the medical system in a country.
 
• **Knowledge**: This dimension is measured by a combination of **Mean Years of Schooling** (for adults aged **25 years** and older) and **Expected Years of Schooling** (for children of school-entering age).
 
• **Decent Standard of Living**: This is measured by **Gross National Income (GNI) per capita** adjusted for **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)** in **US Dollars**.
 
 
 
• **The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**:
 
 
• The **UNDP** was formed on **November 22, 1965**, and is headquartered in **New York City**. It is the leading agency of the **United Nations** focused on international development.
 
• The **Human Development Report (HDR)** has been published by the **UNDP** since **1990** to emphasize that people and their capabilities should be the ultimate criteria for assessing the development of a country.
 
 
 
• **Scoring System**:
 
 
• The **HDI** value ranges between **0 and 1**. Countries with a score of **0.800** or above are categorized as **Very High Human Development**, while those below **0.550** are categorized as **Low Human Development**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Origin of HDI**: The index was created by **Pakistani economist Mahbub ul Haq** and **Indian economist Amartya Sen** in **1990** to shift the focus of development economics from national income accounting to people-centered policies.
 
• **Complementary Indices**: The **HDR** also features other indices such as the **Inequality-adjusted HDI (IHDI)**, the **Gender Development Index (GDI)**, the **Gender Inequality Index (GII)**, and the **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**.
 
• **India's Historical Trend**: Since **1990**, India's **HDI value** has shown a consistent upward trend, largely driven by significant increases in **life expectancy** and **GNI per capita**, despite periodic fluctuations in global rankings.
</ul

questions.question: Who became the first athlete to throw beyond 75 m in the men’s discus event, setting a world record of 75.56 m in April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mykolas Alekna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mykolas Alekna**, a prominent **Lithuanian** athlete, etched his name in sports history by becoming the first individual to throw a discus beyond the **75-meter** mark.
 
• In **April 2025**, during a specialized throwing competition, he recorded a phenomenal distance of **75.56 m**, effectively setting a new **World Record** in the men’s discus event.
 
• The record-breaking performance took place in **Ramona, Oklahoma**, a location frequently chosen by elite throwers for its **favorable wind conditions** that aid in achieving maximum flight for the discus.
 
• This achievement broke a barrier that had long been considered nearly impossible to reach, solidifying **Alekna's** position as one of the greatest talents in modern **Track and Field** history.
 
• At the time of this record, **Mykolas Alekna** was representing the **University of California, Berkeley** in collegiate competitions while competing on the international stage for **Lithuania**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Family Legacy in Athletics:**
 
 
• **Mykolas Alekna** is the son of the legendary **Virgilijus Alekna**, who is a **two-time Olympic champion** (**2000 Sydney** and **2004 Athens**) and a former world record contender himself.
 
• Before **Mykolas** broke the record, **Virgilijus Alekna** held the second-longest throw in history with a mark of **73.88 m**, set in the year **2000**.
 
 
 
• **The Previous World Record:**
 
 
• The men’s discus world record was previously held by **Jürgen Schult** of **East Germany**, who threw **74.08 m** on **June 6, 1986**.
 
• **Schult's** record was one of the **longest-standing records** in men's athletics, lasting for nearly **39 years** before being eclipsed by the **75.56 m** mark.
 
 
 
• **Technical Specifications of the Discus:**
 
 
• In international **senior men's** competitions, the **discus** is a circular plate made of metal or wood with a metal rim, weighing exactly **2 kilograms** (approximately **4.4 lbs**).
 
• The diameter of the men's discus is mandated to be between **219 mm and 221 mm** according to **World Athletics** regulations.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the 75-Meter Barrier:**
 
 
• Much like the **sub-4-minute mile** or the **9.6-second 100m sprint**, the **75-meter** mark in discus was a significant psychological and physical milestone that had eluded athletes for decades.
 
• Achieving this distance requires a perfect combination of **explosive power**, **rotational speed**, and **aerodynamic precision**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geography of the Record:** The town of **Ramona** in **Oklahoma, USA**, has become famous in the athletics world for "The **Oklahoma Throw Series**," where the open fields and steady **updrafts** provide ideal conditions for records to fall.
 
• **Career Highlights:** Before setting the world record, **Mykolas Alekna** had already secured a **Silver medal** at the **2022 World Athletics Championships** at the age of **19** and a **Bronze medal** at the **2023 World Championships**.
 
• **Competition:** Other top athletes mentioned in the options, such as **Matthew Denny** (Australia) and **Sam Mattis** (USA), are also world-class competitors who have consistently reached the finals of major **Olympic** and **World Championship** events.

questions.question: In May 2025, which of the following nodal agencies of the Union Government invited public comments on the Draft Framework of India’s Climate Finance Taxonomy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Department of Economic Affairs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Department of Economic Affairs (DEA)**, which operates under the **Ministry of Finance**, is the nodal agency that invited public comments on the **Draft Framework of India’s Climate Finance Taxonomy** in **May 2025**.
 
• The primary objective of this framework is to provide a comprehensive **classification system** that defines which economic activities can be labeled as "sustainable" or "green" within the **Indian economy**.
 
• By establishing a clear taxonomy, the **Union Government** aims to mobilize large-scale **capital** toward climate-friendly projects while significantly reducing the risk of **greenwashing** in the financial markets.
 
• The draft was developed through extensive consultation with a **task force** that included representatives from the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)**, the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, and the **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)**.
 
• This initiative is a critical step in aligning India's **financial sector** with its international commitments, such as those made under the **Paris Agreement** and the **Panchamrit** targets announced at **COP26**. ***Hence, the correct answer is the Department of Economic Affairs.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Understanding Climate Finance Taxonomy:**
 
 
• A **Taxonomy** acts as a dictionary for **investors**, **banks**, and **policymakers** to identify projects that contribute to **environmental objectives** like **climate change mitigation** and **adaptation**.
 
• The **India-specific taxonomy** focuses on sectors such as **Renewable Energy**, **Energy Efficiency**, **Sustainable Transport**, **Water and Waste Management**, and **Afforestation**.
 
• It helps in the issuance of **Sovereign Green Bonds**, which the **Government of India** began issuing in the **2022-23** financial year to fund **green infrastructure**.
 
 
 
• **Net Zero Target 2070:**
 
 
• India has committed to reaching **Net Zero emissions** by the year **2070**. Achieving this requires an estimated investment of **trillions of dollars** over the coming decades.
 
• The taxonomy ensures that **global and domestic investors** have the transparency needed to invest in **low-carbon technologies** and **resilient infrastructure**.
 
 
 
• **Roles of Other Agencies:**
 
 
• **NITI Aayog:** Acts as the premier **policy think tank** of the Government of India, providing strategic and technical advice but is not the lead for financial regulatory frameworks like the taxonomy.
 
• **National Statistical Office (NSO):** Responsible for the **collection and analysis** of statistical data and the implementation of the **National Sample Survey**.
 
• **Department of Financial Services (DFS):** Handles issues related to **Banking**, **Insurance**, and **Pension Reforms**, supporting the broader fiscal goals of the **Ministry of Finance**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regulatory Convergence:** The **Draft Framework** ensures that **ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance)** reporting by Indian companies is standardized and consistent with **global best practices** like the **EU Taxonomy**.
 
• **Institutional Support:** The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** has also been active in this space, having released a **Framework for Acceptance of Green Deposits** in **2023** to encourage **sustainable finance** at the retail level.
 
• **Economic Impact:** By creating a regulated **green finance ecosystem**, India hopes to attract **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** into **clean energy** sectors, which is vital for maintaining an **8% plus GDP growth rate** while decarbonizing the grid.
